experiment_design.technical_details: This research plan investigates the hypothesis that right-handed Weyl neutrinos are necessary components of matter's fundamental structure, specifically within the context of vector-like regularization in the Standard Model as proposed by Xue (1997). The study focuses on the theoretical consistency of lepton mass generation mechanisms. Since direct detection of right-handed neutrinos is currently beyond experimental reach for many mass ranges, this plan employs a hybrid approach: (1) Re-deriving the theoretical constraints on lepton mass terms using the vector-like regularization framework described in EV-Q075-5c8e119ab0a790ec4aad171b to establish the necessity condition; (2) Constraining the parameter space of such right-handed neutrinos using existing precision data on neutrino oscillations and rare decays, treating the 'necessity' as a model-selection problem between Minimal Standard Model (no right-handed neutrinos) and Extended Vector-Like Models. The core technical challenge is linking the abstract regularization requirement to observable phenomenological signatures.

experiment_design.technical_details: This research plan investigates the hypothesis that right-handed Weyl neutrinos are necessary components of matter's fundamental structure, specifically within the context of vector-like regularization in the Standard Model as proposed by Xue (1997). The study focuses on the theoretical consistency of lepton mass generation mechanisms. Since direct detection of right-handed neutrinos is currently beyond experimental reach for many mass ranges, this plan employs a hybrid approach: (1) Re-deriving the theoretical constraints on lepton mass terms using the vector-like regularization framework described in EV-Q075-5c8e119ab0a790ec4aad171b to establish the necessity condition; (2) Constraining the parameter space of such right-handed neutrinos using existing precision data on neutrino oscillations and rare decays, treating the 'necessity' as a model-selection problem between Minimal Standard Model (no right-handed neutrinos) and Extended Vector-Like Models. The core technical challenge is linking the abstract regularization requirement to observable phenomenological signatures.
